bug_semantics: CWE-200: self-registration hashed the registrant password into Inbox.data and persisted that JSON payload. Inbox index/view (HTML/JSON/CSV) returned the entity unredacted, including the hash; later audit logging also wrote nested password/authkey keys from JSON columns. Privileged inbox/audit readers could recover password hashes for offline cracking. Cerebrate 1.37 redacts those keys at display/audit time while leaving the stored payload intact for account creation.
flaw_origin: 370ae3438e468f168f5793a720125e6d53943bd1 (Sami Mokaddem, 2021-10-20) first implemented live self-registration: UsersController::register() placed the submitted password into the inbox data payload, and RegistrationProcessor::create() hashed it with DefaultPasswordHasher then stored the hash via parent::create()/InboxTable::createEntry(). Parent 43fbdc63f64d6b3295e4f111e494748772ea1d69 already had unredacted inbox data views, but register() was a hardcoded stub without a password field and UserInboxProcessor create() did not hash or store a password. AuditLogBehavior (23dc460359b980becc23be813619a200ade7a822) is a later additional sink, not the first write of the credential material.

reasoning: The security issue is a real CWE-200 disclosure of stored password hashes through existing inbox/audit surfaces. The smallest first write of the sensitive material is 370ae343, which added both the live password into the registration inbox payload and the hash-before-store step. Inbox views already dumped data JSON, so that commit is what made a credential appear in those responses. The BIC object is human-authored with no AI markers; later AI co-authorship on the 2026 redaction fix is irrelevant to BIC attribution. Verdict NOT_AI.
